structured_output.summary: The tip family averages 0.7533 over five runs of the same math, right at the 0.753 gate. The two banked speedups (static shapes −2%, max pool −2.9%) can only be kept if about +0.2 pp of accuracy is found at no time cost. The most relevant outside evidence comes from the two public bs-1536 Muon CIFAR-10 records, hiverge (1.98 s) and Fable e1 (1.828 s). Both share settings that differ from the tip: (1) the whitening bias is trained only for the first 20% of steps, then frozen; (2) the LR decays linearly to a 0.05 floor, holds there for a short tail, and ends with a light EMA over the last ~8 steps (every 4 steps, decay 0.7); (3) BN scales are frozen with eps 1e-12; (4) logits are divided by the feature dimension and the head is initialized normalized by its std; (5) small decoupled weight decay on the orthogonalized filters; (6) LS 0.09, which was already tested and closed here (E037). Point 1 is also a FLOP lever (the group-1 conv1 input gradient is no longer needed after the cutoff). It directly tests H8.1, and the airbench paper says freezing the bias raises throughput without hurting accuracy. Point 2 directly supports testing H6.5.1. Fable found that CUDA graphs and optimizer fusion gave minimal gain under fair retiming, consistent with E052 closing H2.12. MUD (a cheaper orthogonalization) was measured on the airbench Muon script and gave no wall-clock gain while losing 0.7 pp, which closes cheaper-orthogonalizer ideas under H7.2. HTMuon (+0.3 pp on CIFAR-100, long training, SVD-based) and NorMuon (cheap, LLM-only evidence) are low-prior accuracy candidates. A critical-damping momentum schedule costs 1.7 pp on CIFAR-100, consistent with E027's momentum sensitivity. One unresolved discrepancy: a search snippet says L40S and 50 trials, while the repo page and task say A100 PCIe and 40 trials.

findings.claim: Fable's e1 record (1.828 s CIFAR-10, bs 1536) trains the whitening bias only for the first 0.2 epochs ('whiten_bias_epochs': 0.2). The whitening weight is frozen. Its CUDA graphs are keyed by (resolution, whitening_bias_grad, do_norm), so the bias-on and bias-off phases use different graphs.
findings.relevance: This is the bias-learning-rate channel of H8.1 (64x-LR biases hurting early training). It is also a FLOP-saving lever. Once the whitening bias stops training, autograd should no longer need the input gradient of group 1's first conv, which runs at the highest resolution. This is my inference; check whether the tip trains that bias for the whole run. Estimate: ~1-2% of fwd+bwd FLOPs, and it should carry over to the power-capped PCIe judge. Fixed shapes are kept; this needs one extra compiled graph variant, warmed up in build.

findings.claim: airbench: 'The biases are trained for 3 epochs, after which we disable their gradient' to improve throughput without reducing accuracy. Dirac init cut CIFAR-10 SGD from 21 to 18 epochs; lookahead from 13.5 to 12.0 epochs. airbench96 reaches 79.27% on CIFAR-100 without Cutout and 79.76% with it, at long schedules.
findings.relevance: Second independent source that freezing the whitening bias early costs no accuracy and saves time. It strengthens a candidate N-idea: freeze it after 20% of steps on the static-shape + max-pool tip (4.718 s). Cutout's CIFAR-100 gain is at long schedules only, and E008 showed augmentation hurts at ~8 epochs.

findings.claim: Fable e1 LR schedule: decay = max(1 - s*lr2_base, lr_floor), with lr_floor 0.05. The decay ends at 8.5 epochs, but training runs 8.875 epochs, so the last ~0.375 epochs hold at the floor. The EMA starts 8 steps before the decay ends, updates every 4 steps, and blends ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net (foreach_lerp).
findings.relevance: Direct external support for H6.5.1 (Muon floor 0.07 -> 0.05) and its untested variant, a short final EMA. The tip's floor (0.07) and lookahead-EMA ramp were tuned under SGD. Fable spends a floor-held tail instead of decaying to zero, consistent with E015 (decay to 0 hurt). A zero-time version: keep the total step count, end the decay ~4% of steps early, and hold at 0.05 for the rest.

findings.claim: hiverge (1.98 s, bs 1536) settings: Muon lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, Nesterov, norm_freq 2+int(15*progress); weight_decay = 1.0418e-06*batch_size (~1.6e-3 at bs 1536) on the Muon filters; Muon momentum buffer in fp16; SGD momentum 0.825 for biases/BN/head; head_lr 0.5415, bias_lr 0.0573; whitening bias trained for ceil(0.2*len(loader)) steps; BN momentum 0.5566 (PyTorch 1-m), eps 1e-12, BN weight frozen; logits scaled by 1/x.size(-1); whitening via SVD on 960 images; LS 0.09; brightness/contrast jitter; selective TTA (not allowed here).
findings.relevance: A second bs-1536 Muon recipe tuned independently of the tip's lineage. Untested in our tree: decoupled wd on Muon filters (the tip uses renorm instead), BN-scale freezing / eps 1e-12, logit scaling by 1/dim, and the 20% whitening-bias cutoff. An fp16 Muon momentum buffer halves momentum memory traffic. That is a tiny but math-near-neutral saving in the per-step Muon cost (H7.2).

findings.claim: Fable e1 head: 'return self.head(x) / x.size(-1)' (logits divided by the feature dimension), head weight initialized normalized by w.std(), and head on SGD with lr 0.5415.
findings.relevance: Relevant to H7.3 (why head-on-Muon gave +0.32 pp). In tuned CIFAR-10 Muon recipes the head stays on SGD, at a high LR with a 1/dim logit scale. So the head's effective step size, not orthogonalization, is a plausible mechanism. H7.3.1's step-size-matched SGD head is the clean test.

findings.claim: Fable e1 is 7.6% faster than hiverge (1.828 vs 1.978 s). The 28->32 curriculum gave -0.128 s and extending to 24->28->32 another -0.081 s. CUDA graphs and optimizer fusion 'provided minimal measurable gains under fair retiming'. GlobalAmaxPool replaced the original pool because low-res training needed a true global pool.
findings.relevance: Agrees with E052 (GPU busy 98-100%, so CUDA graphs are closed) and with E056 (pool replacement is a real lever). Note that E055 found amax backward NaNs under torch 2.4 Inductor fp16. Fable's amax pool presumably runs on a newer torch, so keep max(dim).values. Supports retiring H2.12.1 and H2.12.2.

findings.claim: MUD (triangular/Cholesky-like momentum decorrelation, Q <- T^-1 Q with T = tril(QQ^T)) on the public airbench Muon script, Table 6, 20 runs. At 8 epochs: MUD1 93.34% in 2.98 s vs Muon5 94.03% in 3.04 s. At 13 epochs: 94.07% in 4.75 s vs 94.44% in 4.82 s. Authors: 'MUD does not retain a meaningful per-run wall-clock advantage over Muon' on CNNs, because NS GEMMs on small matrices are already efficient.
findings.relevance: Closes 'cheaper orthogonalizer' levers for this small-CNN regime, consistent with E031/E033 (orthogonalization quality is an accuracy knob; 3 NS steps is saturated). It also lowers the prior for H7.2.4 (AOL + 2 iterations).

findings.claim: HTMuon replaces U V^T with U Sigma^p V^T (p=0.125). On CIFAR-100 ResNet18 it gives 78.24% vs Muon 77.95% (+0.29 pp); ResNet50 80.16% vs 79.85%; on CIFAR-10 +0.16-0.24 pp. It needs an SVD, or an NS-approximation variant, or applying it every N steps. All results use long training.
findings.relevance: One of the few published Muon variants with a CIFAR-100 accuracy gain, but only under long schedules. Our 3-step NS already leaves small singular values partly unequalized (E033: 56% in [0.7, 1.3]), and NS 4 gave nothing. A low-prior accuracy candidate for H7; only worth an offline spectrum check, not a scored run.

findings.claim: NorMuon adds a row-wise (per-neuron) second-moment EMA (beta2 0.95), applied after orthogonalization, with LR rescaled by 0.2*sqrt(mn)/||O||_F. Overhead is negligible (an extra m-vector; ~2.9% step time vs AdamW in LLMs). It reports +11.31% step efficiency over Muon at 1.1B. The paper has no CNN or CIFAR experiments.
findings.relevance: A cheap elementwise addition to the compiled Muon update. It could be a zero-time accuracy source (H6/H7) by equalizing per-filter update scale, but there is no CNN evidence, and the tip's per-filter renorm may already do this job. Low-to-moderate prior.

findings.claim: A critical-damping momentum schedule mu(t) = 1 - 2*sqrt(alpha(t)) reaches 90% on CIFAR-10 2.34x faster but ends 0.46 pp lower. On CIFAR-100 the final-accuracy cost grows to -1.7 pp, so the matched-accuracy gain drops to 1.14x.
findings.relevance: External support that momentum schedules are risky on CIFAR-100 at a fixed target, consistent with E027 (Muon momentum 0.85: -1.18 pp) and E030 (flat 0.5-0.6). Do not reopen momentum schedules.

findings.claim: A search-result snippet reports that adding decoupled weight decay of 5e-4 to Muon on CIFAR-10 gave 94.46% vs 94.12% without it. The originating paper is unclear among the results (arxiv 2607.29674 / 2607.26001); the setting is longer training.
findings.relevance: Weak evidence that wd on Muon parameters adds accuracy. The tip's head-on-Muon group has no wd or renorm (E044 note). Adding small decoupled wd to the Muon head (or matching hiverge's ~1.6e-3 on the filters) is a zero-time candidate for H7.3 / H6. Unverified source; treat as a prior only.

findings.claim: Benchmark repo: a ResNet9 baseline (verified 2026-10-02) scores 75.36% in 59.30 s. Official judging: A100 80GB PCIe, 40 trials, mean >=75%, eval <=5 s untimed. A search snippet on the same repo instead says 'L40S 48GB and 50 fresh training trials'. The futurebiohackers PR #3 (8.11 s, 75.29%) is now 404; its snippet says 'Muon lost to SGD at every size' in their CIFAR-100 tests.
findings.relevance: The judge spec has an unresolved discrepancy (A100 PCIe/40 vs L40S/50, maybe an older version). It matters for which levers transfer: power-capped FLOP levers vs per-step levers. The futurebiohackers claim against Muon is contradicted by E019/E044, confirming that external negative priors are weak.
